nodes.name: Lemma 3.4, Section 3, Lemma 4.1: § iii $\#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\le F_{d}(c_u(A))$
nodes.statement:
Let \(v:S\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N_S}\) be the fixed embedding
(8), let \(D(S,v)\) be defined by
(10), and retain the functions \(H_N\) of
Lemma~2.4.
For every \(N,D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), there is a nondecreasing function
\(F_{N,D}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) such that, if \(N_S=N\) and \(D(S,v)\le D\), then
\[
        \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\le F_{N,D}(c_{w_v}(A))
        \qquad(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_{m,S},\overline{\mathbb}{Q}_{\ell})).
\]
Choosing \(g_{N,D}\) as in Lemma~3.1, one may take
\[
        F_{N,D}(t)=2H_N(g_{N,D}t)^2.
\]
The function \(F_{N,D}\) is independent of \(\bar k\) and of \(\ell\).

For every \(d\ge1\), there is a nondecreasing function
\(F_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), independent of the algebraically closed base field and of
\(\ell\), with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] for \(M\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), with \(\mathcal{H}^i(M)_1\) the stalks at the identity,
\[
        \sum_ic_u({}^pH^i(M))\le F_{d}(c_u(M)),\qquad
        \sum_i\dim\mathcal{H}^i(M)_1\le F_{d}(c_u(M)).
\]
\item[(ii)] for semisimple \(M\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\),
\[
        c_u(M\oplus M^\vee)\le F_{d}(c_u(M)).
\]
\item[(iii)] if \(d\ge2\), then for every perverse sheaf \(A\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and every Kummer character
\(\lambda\) of the first factor, using the notation in (11)
\[
\begin{gathered}
        \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\le F_{d}(c_u(A)),\\
        c_u(B_{!,\lambda}),\ c_u(B_{*,\lambda}),\
        c_u({}^pH^r(B_{!,\lambda})),\ c_u({}^pH^r(B_{*,\lambda}))
        \le F_{d}(c_u(A))
        \qquad(r\in\mathbb Z).
\end{gathered}
\]
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1: counting $\Delta(K)$
nodes.statement:
For every \(d\ge1\) there is a nondecreasing function
\(\Phi^\Delta_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with the following property.  For every
\(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every
\(K\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\overline{\mathbb}{Q}_{\ell})\) with \(c_u(K)\le C\), and every \(n\ge1\),
\[
        |\Delta(K)(k_n)|\le \Phi^\Delta_{d}(C)\,q^{n(d-1)} .
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2: stratified vanishing
nodes.statement:
For every \(d\ge1\) there is a nondecreasing function
\(\Psi_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) such that for every \(C\ge0\), every finite field
\(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every \(A\in\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\overline{\mathbb}{Q}_{\ell})\) with
\(c_u(A)\le C\), every \(0\le i\le d\), and every \(n\ge1\),
\[
        |\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)(k_n)|\le\Psi_{d}(C)\,q^{n(d-i)} .
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 3.3: perverse amplitude
nodes.statement:
If \(F\) is a perverse sheaf on \(\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\), then
\[
        Rp_!F\in{}^pD^{[0,1]}(S),
        \qquad
        Rp_*F\in{}^pD^{[-1,0]}(S).
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3: unramified locus
nodes.statement:
For every \(d\ge1\) there is a nondecreasing function
\(\Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with the following property.  For
every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime
\(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every arithmetically semisimple object
\(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) whose geometric base change
\(M=M_{0,\bar k}\) satisfies \(c_u(M)\le C\), and every \(n\ge1\),
\[
        |(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\overline{\mathbb}{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X(M_0))(k_n)|
        \le \Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C)\,q^{n(d-1)} .
\]

nodes.name: Corollary 1.4: equidistribution
nodes.statement:
Assume that \(\sup_jc_u(M_j)<\infty\), that \(r_j=r\) for some integer \(r\), and that
\(G_j^{\mathrm{ari}}=G_j^{\mathrm{geo}}\) for every \(j\).  Suppose that these groups are conjugate in
\(\operatorname{GL}_{r,\overline{\mathbb}{Q}_{\ell}}\) to a fixed reductive subgroup \(G\).  After choosing such conjugacies,
the unitary Frobenius conjugacy classes \(\Theta_{M_{j,0},k_j}(\chi)\), \(\chi\in X_j\), become
\(\mu_G^\sharp\)-equidistributed in \(K_G^\sharp\) as \(j\to\infty\).
